question: Prediction of conversion from MCI to AD/dementia among ADNI MCI participants from cognitive tests plus structural MRI measures. Same task and population class. The shared channels are cognitive tests and MRI (P-186: 8 neuropsychological measures plus FreeSurfer MRI markers; P-156: cognitive tests, FreeSurfer MRI volumes/ROI measures, CSF, demographics and APOE). Allowed differences: input (two observed visits plus a forecast value vs baseline only), outcome window (conversion before month 36 vs most recent diagnosis), cohort subset, features, sample size and validation design.

figures.P-186: NM+MRI, 1-year-ahead: AUC 0.957, 5-fold CV, n=85 (35 MCIp, 50 MCIs); no interval reported. Hanley-McNeil with n1=35, n2=50: Q1=0.9175, Q2=0.9360, SE=0.0249, 95% CI 0.908-1.000 (capped). 6-month-ahead: AUC 0.912, n=119 (49/70), SE 0.0297, 95% CI 0.854-0.970.
figures.P-156: EI (stacking with random forest) AUC 0.81 on a held-out random 20% test set of the 841-patient cohort (288 progressed, 553 stayed MCI); test class sizes not reported, expected about 58/110 from the 20% split. Hanley-McNeil with n1=58, n2=110: Q1=0.6807, Q2=0.7250, SE=0.0377, 95% CI 0.736-0.884.
figures.comparison: The intervals do not overlap (0.908-1.000 vs 0.736-0.884). Each estimate lies outside the other's interval, and P-186's 6-month-ahead 0.912 (0.854-0.970) also excludes 0.81 and lies outside P-156's interval.

matched_figure_check: No figure is reported under the other paper's condition. P-186 has no baseline-only result: all its figures use two observed visits plus a forecast value. P-156 uses baseline data only and reports no longitudinal model. P-156's per-modality results appear only as cross-validation distributions in Fig. 3, with no numbers in the text. Nothing reconciles the pair. Condition 3 holds.
performance_validity: Passes condition 5: 0.957 (n=85, internal 5-fold CV, no external cohort) is below 0.97, and P-156's 0.81 is far below. P-186's figure is optimistic: features are scaled on the whole dataset before splitting, markers are ranked on baseline readings, and the reported marker-subset size is the best of those tried. This is recorded as a candidate explanation, not an exclusion.

candidate_explanations.difference: Input representation: P-186 classifies trajectories of two observed visits plus a forecast value at the time of conversion; P-156 uses baseline data only. P-186 attributes its AUC mainly to the forecast value but reports no baseline-only or two-visit-only comparator, so this is not shown to be sufficient.
candidate_explanations.quote: method proposed in this paper has recorded the highest classiﬁcation AUC of 95.7% predominantly because of involving the forecasted marker value at the time of conversion as a classiﬁcation feature.
based only on data collected at baseline when they were diagnosed with MCI

candidate_explanations.difference: Outcome window: conversion before month 36 (P-186) vs most recent recorded diagnosis with no fixed horizon (P-156).
candidate_explanations.quote: The most recent diagnosis given to each patient (Final DX) was the outcome predicted (stable MCI or progressed to dementia).

candidate_explanations.difference: Cohort subset and sample size: an ADNI-1 MCI subsample with three consecutive annual readings (n=85) vs all baseline early/late MCI in ADNI 1/2/GO through TADPOLE (n=841, test set about 168).
candidate_explanations.quote: for 1-year-ahead prediction, the dataset contains three consecutive annual readings, resulting in 35 MCIp and 50 MCIs subjects

candidate_explanations.difference: Validation: 5-fold CV with features scaled before the split and the best marker-subset size reported (P-186) vs one random 80/20 held-out split (P-156).
candidate_explanations.quote: We scale all features to have values between 0 and 1 before the train-test split.

candidate_explanations.difference: Feature set and missing-data handling: P-156 adds CSF, demographics and APOE, drops modalities with 30% or more missing values (including PET and DTI), and imputes the rest by KNN.
candidate_explanations.quote: Several of the TADPOLE data modalities consisted of features that were missing for at least 30 % of the MCI patients

reason: Both papers predict MCI-to-AD/dementia conversion in ADNI MCI from cognitive tests plus MRI measures and report AUC. P-186's 0.957 (derived CI 0.908-1.000) and P-156's 0.81 (derived CI 0.736-0.884) do not overlap. Neither paper reports a result under the other's input condition that would reconcile them. The pair qualifies. The candidate explanations (P-186's longitudinal forecast-value input, the outcome window, the cohort subset, P-186's optimistic validation, and the feature sets) are not shown to be sufficient.
